evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: "Best practices in code quality, data modeling, testing, and monitoring", "operational responsibilities", "SLOs" all point to rigour; however "pragmatically refactor" softens it — they don't want paralysis by perfectionism.
evidence.domain_risk: "Reliable, high-quality datasets/pipelines", "SLOs", "monitoring" — production reliability is the primary concern, but domain is travel marketplace (consumer product), not financial reporting or a regulated industry.
evidence.jd_authorship: "Expertise in SQL & Python, building robust data pipelines and data models", "experience operating data at scale in warehouses/lakes (Delta, Snowflake, PostgreSQL/MySQL)", "maintain balance between operational responsibilities and new development using team SLOs" show technical depth; "proactive ownership mindset with customer orientation" and "excellent English communication skills (written and verbal)" are generic recruiter-facing framing.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: "Improve what's already in production: Pragmatically refactor and simplify existing pipelines" is a named responsibility. "Build end-to-end data solutions" adds some greenfield scope, but the weight of the role is on maintaining and improving existing systems.
evidence.data_team_maturity: "Traveler Data Engineering" named as the specific team in the job title — implies a named sub-team within a larger data organisation. "Maintain balance between operational responsibilities and new development using team SLOs" signals a team with defined SLOs, live production systems, and structured operational processes.
evidence.collaboration_width: Named verbatim: "Product" and "Data teams" (named explicitly in "thought partner with Product and Data teams to translate business requirements"). "Code reviews, and knowledge sharing" implies peer engineers as a third group.
evidence.language_gate: "Excellent English communication skills (written and verbal)" is stated as a required qualification — hard gate for English. No second language requirement stated.
